title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Fig. 2a (legend and panel a); Methods 'Optogenetic stimulation system and approach'
quote: MDN (backwards walking, n = 9 flies, 271 trials). Control: no DN expression (n = 3 flies, 47 trials).
mapping_basis: Paper name MDN is the MANC type name MDN; split line SS03131 is listed as MDN in driver_lines.csv and in the paper's Supplementary Table 2.
stimulation: 640-nm laser focused on the neck connective, 21 uW, 5-s stimulation periods interleaved with 10-s rest
sensory_condition: tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill; dorsal thorax opened for two-photon imaging of the cervical connective
penetrance: backward walking probability rises during stimulation (Fig. 2a)
n_flies_note: 9 flies, 271 trials; only trials in which the fly was walking in the 1 s before stimulation were analysed
notes: Backward walking coded yes for all leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3. Trials were preselected for walking before stimulus; forward velocity becomes negative (backward walking) during stimulation. Paper says the MDN-spGAL4 is MDN3 from Bidaye 2014 and drives cell-specific expression. Combined calcium imaging experiment (Dfd-LexA>GCaMP6s).

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
quote: (iii) walk backward upon MDN stimulation for stimuli ≥ 10.5 μW
mapping_basis: Paper name MDN is the MANC type name MDN; split line SS03131 is listed as MDN in driver_lines.csv and in the paper's Supplementary Table 2.
stimulation: 640-nm laser at 2.3, 10.5, 21 and 41.6 uW on the neck (d); 21 uW on the anterior dorsal thorax, neck or head (e); 5-s stimulation
penetrance: reliable backward walking at >= 10.5 uW; little or no effect at 2.3 uW
n_flies_note: panel d: 4 flies, 50 trials per condition; panel e: 3 flies, 30 trials per condition
notes: Intensity series (d) and stimulation site series (e). Panel e legend: MDN stimulation elicits backward walking when illuminating the anterior dorsal thorax, the neck or the head. Strongest clearly reported condition used; the lowest intensity (2.3 uW) did not reliably drive backward walking.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Fig. 4d (black traces, intact); main text section 'Behavioural requirement of DN recruitment'
quote: stimulation of DNp09, aDN2 and MDN in intact animals drove forwards walking, antennal grooming and backwards walking, respectively (Fig. 4b–d, black traces)
mapping_basis: Paper name MDN is the MANC type name MDN; split line SS03131 is listed as MDN in driver_lines.csv and in the paper's Supplementary Table 2.
stimulation: 640-nm laser, 21 uW, focused on the anterior dorsal thorax, 5-s stimulation, 10 trials per fly
penetrance: backward walking probability peaks at about 0.6-0.7 during stimulation (Fig. 4d)
notes: The same animals were then decapitated (see record a5-g11b-A-0004). Backward walking coded yes for all leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Fig. 4d (blue traces, headless); main text section 'Behavioural requirement of DN recruitment'; Supplementary Table 5
quote: After decapitating these same animals, we found that the activation of MDN in headless flies still drove backwards walking.
mapping_basis: Paper name MDN is the MANC type name MDN; split line SS03131 is listed as MDN in driver_lines.csv and in the paper's Supplementary Table 2.
stimulation: 640-nm laser, 21 uW, focused on the anterior dorsal thorax, 5-s stimulation, 10 trials per fly
sensory_condition: decapitated, neck sealed with UV glue, on spherical treadmill (also 10 trials hanging without ground contact, Supplementary Video 3)
penetrance: backward walking probability not significantly different from intact (P = 0.265)
notes: Headless backward walking on the ball, quantified by ball velocity and a behaviour classifier. Backward walking coded yes for all leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3. The hanging, no-ground-contact headless condition is shown only in Supplementary Video 3, which is not in the room, so it is not coded.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 10b (black traces, intact legs); Discussion; Supplementary Table 6
quote: We found that MDN-driven backwards walking only depends on active movements of the two hindlegs57 (Extended Data Fig. 10b and Supplementary Video 6)
mapping_basis: Paper name MDN is the MANC type name MDN; split line SS03131 is listed as MDN in driver_lines.csv and in the paper's Supplementary Table 2.
stimulation: 640-nm laser, 21 uW, 5-s stimulation, 10 trials before and 10 after amputation, 25 s between stimuli
sensory_condition: tethered on spherical treadmill; tested before and after bilateral hindleg amputation at the tibia-tarsus joint
coordination_notes: After bilateral hindleg amputation (tibia-tarsus), backward displacement was abolished (intact vs amputated P = 0.010; amputated MDN vs amputated control n.s.), so backward propulsion depends on active hindleg movement.
n_flies_note: 4 intact-leg MDN flies, 5 hindleg-amputated MDN flies (Supplementary Table 6)
notes: Leg codes refer to flies with intact legs, whose cumulative backward displacement (about -6 mm over 5 s) is shown in the figure. Legend: 'Amputation of the hind legs is sufficient to prevent flies from walking backward upon MDN optogenetic stimulation.' The amputated condition was not coded separately because the paper attributes the residual movement to struggle-associated noise and does not describe front- or mid-leg stepping.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5a (black traces, intact); main text section 'Network size predicts behavioural necessity'
quote: DNp42 has monosyaptic connections to 29 other DNs and triggers backing up in intact animals64.
mapping_basis: Paper name DNp42 is the MANC type name DNp42 (unambiguous in type_list.csv); line SS57807 maps to DNp42 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 640-nm laser, 21 uW, 5-s stimulation, 10 trials per fly, 25 s between trials, holder filled with saline
penetrance: mean fictive forward velocity drops to about -1 mm/s during stimulation (intact vs headless P = 0.040)
notes: 'Backing up' / 'backwards retreat' coded as backward walking, so yes for all leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3. Evidence is ball velocity only; Supplementary Video 4 is not available here. Confidence is medium because n = 3 and legs were not tracked. The paper chose lines where a clean spGAL4 was available. Controls were Canton S background.

title: Descending networks transform command signals into population motor control.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 5a (blue traces, headless); main text section 'Network size predicts behavioural necessity'
quote: This behavior is not observed in headless flies, as quantified by fictive forward walking velocity.
mapping_basis: Paper name DNp42 is the MANC type name DNp42 (unambiguous in type_list.csv); line SS57807 maps to DNp42 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 640-nm laser, 21 uW, 5-s stimulation, 10 trials per fly
sensory_condition: decapitated, neck sealed, on spherical treadmill (no hanging condition for DNp42 per Supplementary Video 4 legend)
penetrance: headless DNp42 vs headless control fictive forward velocity not different (P = 0.191)
notes: Backward retreat was lost after decapitation; the fictive forward velocity trace is flat. The paper describes no other leg movement for headless DNp42 flies. Legs were coded no for stepping on the basis of ball velocity only (Supplementary Video 4 is not available here), so confidence is medium.
